name: The World
upright: The CIA triad designed in from the first requirement: least privilege, layered defense, secure defaults, failing closed.
reversed: Security bolted on at the end: default passwords, flat trust, complexity nobody can review, a cloud nobody thought was theirs.
vision: A dancer spins inside an oval wreath woven from many separate hedges; slip through one and the next still holds. They carry two wands, one to sign and one to pay, and may never raise both at once. When the music stops, every gate in the wreath swings shut. At the dancer's heart glows a sealed crystal that remembers each step since dawn and will shine in no other body. In the corners, the eagle mends only its half of a nest rented in the sky; the bull drags a plow no one may stop to repair; the lion wears a collar still set to its factory password; the angel has no body, only a voice.
decode: A wreath of many separate hedges → defense in depth: layered, varied controls, so one failed layer does not mean a breach.
Two wands never raised together; gates that shut when the music stops → separation of duties: no one completes a critical task alone; fail securely: default to closed.
A crystal heart that remembers every step and shines in no other body → TPM: a chip bound to one motherboard that stores keys and measures the boot.
The eagle mending half a rented nest; the bull's unstoppable plow → cloud shared responsibility; ICS puts availability first and is hard to patch.
The lion's factory-password collar; the bodiless angel → IoT ships with default credentials; serverless has no server to harden, but code and permissions stay yours.
facts: In IaaS the customer secures the OS, apps and data; in PaaS, apps and data; in SaaS, mainly data and access. The customer stays accountable for its data in all three.
VM escape lets code break out of a guest to the hypervisor and other guests; containers share the host kernel, so one kernel flaw can expose them all.
A TPM is a chip bound to one device for measured boot and disk keys; an HSM is a separate, tamper-resistant device that generates, stores and uses many keys at speed.
trap: The collective's oldest regret is bolting security on after the build. It belongs in the first requirements and every phase through retirement; a flaw fixed in design costs a fraction of one fixed in production.
